name: AD823 / AD823A
tagline: ADI's 1995 JFET dual that runs from 3 V: a CMoy favourite Tangent found punchier and more detailed than OPA132/134.

lineage.note: Sole source, CB process; datasheet 00901 Rev. 0 (5/95) to E (11/11). Leaded codes retired via PDN 10_0081, PDN 16_0062.
PCN 26_0029 moves AD823ANZ/ARZ wafers to Camas; no fit/form/function change expected. Previous fab unnamed.
New XFCB die, same dual pinout and 3–36 V supply; SOIC/MSOP only. Datasheet D09439.

part_numbers.note: Leaded PDIP-8; probably dropped by PDN 10_0081 Rev. B (replacement AD823ANZ). Absent from Rev. E.
RoHS PDIP-8, the rollers' part. In PCN 26_0029. Digi-Key AD823ANZ-ND, Farnell 1438581.
Leaded SOIC-8, original die; probably discontinued by PDN 16_0062. 'A' is temperature grade.
RoHS SOIC-8, original die, since Rev. A (5/04). ARZ in PCN 26_0029; reels unconfirmed.
AD823A (2012 XFCB die) SOIC-8; different silicon from AD823ARZ. LCSC C652580.
AD823A MSOP-8, branding H34. EVBs AD823A-2AR-EBZ and AD823A-2ARM-EBZ.

reputation.summary: A 2000s favourite for battery CMoy portables. Tangent found it punchier and more detailed than the OPA134/132, ideal on 3 V, but too aggressive with forward headphones and short on current. Soomal cites a warm, dynamic reputation and found it in early Graham Slee SOLO amps and the Colorfly C4 Pro and Hidizs AP100 DAPs. No ASR or Groner measurements.
typical_uses: Battery CMoy / portable headphone amps on 3 V
Graham Slee SOLO (earlier versions, per Soomal)
DAPs: Colorfly C4 Pro; Hidizs AP100 (role unconfirmed)
Op-amp rolling in DIY and commercial DAC/amps
ADI 3 V headphone circuit (−62 dB THD+N, 32 Ω)
caveats: Low output current (15–17 mA, 0.5 V from rails); weak into low-impedance headphones without a buffer.
Offset much higher on ±15 V (3.5 mV max vs 0.8 mV at 5 V).
Inputs beyond +VS by 300 mV or with supplies off need a series resistor (1 kΩ withstands 10 V).
About 20° phase margin into 470 pF as follower; add a series output resistor. Only AD823ANZ comes in DIP.
Post-2026 stock comes from Camas fab; not guaranteed identical silicon. Reputation is mostly subjective.

counterfeit_notes: No AD823 counterfeit reports found. Inferences: recent-date-code 'AD823AN' DIPs deserve scrutiny; an 'AD823A' DIP is mislabelled or fake; check full order code (AD823ARZ vs AD823AARZ) and datasheet (D00901 vs D09439). Post-2026 Camas parts may differ slightly yet be genuine.

silicon_changes.summary: PCN 26_0029, 'Qualification of ADI Camas Wafer Fab CB Processes', moves Complementary Bipolar production to the existing qualified Camas, WA process, with 'no expected impact to fit, form, function or reliability'. AD823ANZ and AD823ARZ are listed. Same part numbers; no die-layout change stated. Issue and implementation dates unconfirmed.
silicon_changes.identification: Not confirmed; ADI usually separates stock by date code or lot. Part number, marking and datasheet (Rev. E) are unchanged.

spec_deltas.before: previous ADI fab (not named in the sources seen)
spec_deltas.after: ADI Camas, WA fab (existing qualified CB process)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown; datasheet limits unchanged and no comparisons exist. Record date codes if you prize older AD823ANZ stock.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: no fit/form/function impact stated, datasheet unchanged; matters mainly for matched pairs.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN title and wording confirmed; the AD823ANZ/ARZ listing rests on a single summary.

silicon_changes.summary: ADI introduced a materially different die under a near-identical name, alongside rather than replacing the original. AD823A uses the XFCB dielectrically isolated process with a two-stage folded-cascode design; AD823 uses the CB process with a nested integrator. Same pinout and supply; specs, output drive and packages differ.
silicon_changes.identification: Double-A order codes (AD823AARZ vs AD823ARZ); SOIC_N and MSOP only, MSOP branding H34; datasheet D09439 vs D00901. Listings saying only 'AD823A' are ambiguous.

spec_deltas.before: CB process, nested integrator, complementary common-emitter RRO
spec_deltas.after: XFCB (dielectrically isolated), two-stage with folded-cascode first stage, RRO

spec_deltas.parameter: Slew rate (5 V, G=-1, 4 V step)
Linear output current, 0.5 V from rails
Ib typ, and max at TMAX (5 V)

spec_deltas.after: -108 dBc SFDR (G = -1, RF = RG = 4 kΩ); -99 dBc (G = +1, RL = 1 kΩ); test conditions differ

silicon_changes.audio_impact: No listening reports. On paper ~2.5× the output current, lower noise, faster slew. The praised sound comes from the original PDIP part.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: same SOIC pinout, no DIP; different compensation; input CM ±VS ± 0.7 V; 30 V overheating caution.
silicon_changes.verification: Datasheet-backed; classed as successor because the AD823A has distinct order codes.

revision_history.changes: Specs, ordering guide, outline updated; Pb-free ARZ/-RL/-R7 added. Differential input abs max ±1.2 V; ±15 V table had unit errors.
New format; DC Performance (p.5), outline and ordering guide changed. ±15 V unit fixes probably here.
Table 4 (Absolute Maximum Ratings) changed; probably differential input ±1.2 V → ±VS.
Figure 34 (pulse response, CL = 470 pF) and Figure 36 (simplified schematic) changed.
Editorial Theory of Operation changes; ordering guide drops AD823AN. Tables numerically identical to Rev. A. Still current after PCN 26_0029.
Initial version of the AD823A (new XFCB part).
Added caution about overheating from output current at 30 V supply; Equation 8 changed.

claims_confirmed: ADI AD823 URL serves 'Dual, 16 MHz, Rail-to-Rail FET Input Amplifier AD823 Rev. E' (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/AD823.pdf).
−108 dB THD at 20 kHz, 22 V/µs, 2.6 mA per amplifier (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad823.pdf).
AD823A datasheet 'Wide Supply Dual, 17 MHz…' (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/AD823A.pdf) is Revision B (https://www.radiolocman.com/datasheet/pdf.html?di=171865).
PCN 26_0029 uses the qualified Camas, WA process, no expected fit/form/function/reliability impact (https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/8933/ADI_PCN_26_0029_Rev_-_Form.pdf).
AD823ANZ and AD823ARZ listed in PCN 26_0029 (https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/4778405.pdf).

PDN 16_0062 and PDN 10_0081 Rev. B reference AD823 codes with replacements (https://media.digikey.com/pdf/PCNs/Analog%20Devices/ADI_PDN_16_0062_Rev_-_Form.pdf, https://www.analog.com/media/en/pcn/ADI_PDN_10_0081_Rev_B_Form.pdf).
refuted_claims: 'No PCN or fab transfer for the AD823' is refuted: PCN 26_0029 (2026) moves AD823ANZ and AD823ARZ to Camas, WA (https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/8933/ADI_PCN_26_0029_Rev_-_Form.pdf).
